answer: Each identity consigns one distinct pallet of perishable grove produce, sealed with an ivory tag and logged by a cold-store mirror camera that posts hourly temperature hashes. Verifiers match tag, weight loss and buyer receipts; spoiled or unsold stock is charged to the holder and a second spoilage revokes the slot. One pallet costs $380 plus $45 weekly cold rent, so 1,000 Sybils tie up $425,000 in stock that rots in 21 days and needs real buyers per fake. Trade-off: seasonal supply limits admission and food waste is real.
